entry.title: ACHE: What Kind of Life Is This? ☕
entry.summary: For those who are still here — without really knowing why. Some books promise answers. This one doesn’t. ACHE: What Kind of Life Is This? is a quiet piece of fiction by Cahyanudien Aziz Saputra about something smaller — and maybe more honest. It’s about continuing. You wake up. Nothing big. Just a normal day. But somehow… something is slightly wrong. Not enough to call it a disaster. Just enough to make the day feel a little off. The bus arrives a little late. And the strange thing is — Quietly. Most stories are about big things. Winning. But many lives aren’t like that. Many lives exist in a quieter space — ACHE was written from that space. It isn’t a book trying to fix your life. It’s a book that simply sits beside it. This is not a book about becoming better. It’s not a book about productivity or mindset. There are no lessons at the end. No grand message. Instead, it follows someone moving through a city that rarely notices he exists. And somehow… that might feel familiar. In everyday life, I work as a developer building systems used by thousands of people. Systems are logical. You write code. But human life rarely behaves like that. Sometimes things go wrong for reasons nobody planned. And yet people keep moving forward anyway. ACHE was written in that quiet space — logic and silence. This book might resonate with you if you have ever: waited somewhere until your number was already gone arrived somewhere only to find it closed felt exhausted by endless advice about “staying positive” continued living without fully knowing why Not every life becomes a story about victory. Some lives simply… continue. And maybe that is already something. If you’re curious, you can read more here: 🌐 Official page https://www.cahyanudien.site/ache-what-kind-of-life-is-this/ 📱 Kindle (Amazon) https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GS224DVW 📖 Google Play Books https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=9dTHEQAAQBAJ 🎥 About the book here (Indonesian): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TdQlQ9jzBZo Rei walks. Maybe you do too. 🚶‍♂️

entry.title: Why self-assessment is broken (and how I fixed it with binary evidence)
entry.summary:
The Problem
Last month I tried to honestly assess my skills as a solopreneur. The standard approach: list your skills, rate them 1-5. Have I ranked a page on Google’s 1st page? No. Have I done keyword research + published optimized content? No. Have I intentionally built backlinks? No. That 4 was a fantasy. Dunning-Kruger in action, we overrate the skills we're weakest at because we don't know enough to know what we don't know. The fix is simple: replace "how good am I?" with "what have I actually done?" Done keyword research and published optimized content? Binary. No room for ego. You either have the evidence or you don't. I turned this into proofwork, an evidence-based skill tracker for solopreneurs. Think - Are you validating before building? Do you have a pricing strategy? Are you tracking metrics? Build - Can you ship frontend, backend, and infrastructure? Are you using AI and automation to multiply your output? Sell - Can you write copy that converts? Do you understand SEO? Can you build an audience? Sustain - Do you have your legal and financial house in order? Are you managing your energy sustainably? The app lets you export your current state as a JSON file: proofwork-2026-03.json. Other features: Share your map via URL (state encoded in hash, no server needed) Gap analysis view auto-ranks your weakest skills Radar visualization across all branches Notes field for reflections (saved in the JSON) 100% client-side — your data never leaves your browser After filling it out honestly: Build: ~79% - good, but gaps in testing Sell: ~28% - almost nothing proven Think: ~28% - had never validated an idea properly Sustain: ~55% - no business entity, but good bookkeeping I was spending 90% of my time in the one pillar that was already my strongest (build).
